137	## POSITIONS and FACTS
138	
139	POSITIONS and FACTS describe the present: no dates, no names of who found what, no "corrected" or "superseded" notes. The history of each entry is in `POSITIONS-history.md` and `FACTS-history.md`, beside them. When your work needs the detail of an entry, print the report section that it cites (`$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'`, below). Read its history only when the tree disagrees with the entry.
140	
141	Each entry is one line that starts with its permanent number: `F-87` in FACTS, `P-48` in POSITIONS. A FACTS entry is the fact as it stands now, what it means for the work, and the test that fails if the fact stops holding, under a bold title. If no test checks the fact, the entry gives the command and the output that show it. It points to the report section that holds the detail. Cite an entry by its number. If the reader must know what the entry says without printing it, add the first words of its title in quotes: F-87, "The first words ...".

143	## The gap ledger
144	
145	The ledger's rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).
146	
147	A row is one line of eight cells, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of a topic section. Reports cite a row by its number, which it keeps for good. A new issue gets a new row.
148	
149	- Its status is one of seven words: `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`, `FIXED`, `DUPLICATE`. The last three close a row. The row template (below) defines each.
150	- Its class is a kind and an area, such as `implementation gap (checker)`.
151	- The earlier text of a changed row is in `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`.
152	
153	Read the ledger only through the queries below: it is too large to read whole.
154	
155	A row states its gap as it stands now. A note adds a fact. If your work changes what a row says, write the row's whole new line with `rewrite` (below), not a note that tells the repair.
156	
157	The heading reader of `ledger.py` does not expand the specification's `\Trait{X}` macro. So a row that names a library trait's section cites `Specification-1.0-frozen/` by line.

159	## Reading the record
160	
161	Read only the slice of the record that you need. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:
162

164	
165	- `$T 'F-87'` prints one entry by its number, and `$T 'P-48'` one of POSITIONS. `$T 'F-87+'` adds each entry that F-87 cites by its number, and each entry that cites F-87. `$T 'history:F-87'` prints its history. Run one when your brief or a note cites an entry by its number.
166	- `$T 'positions:WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints one of the curator's decisions. Run it before you choose among ways to do something. If several titles hold the words, it names them.
167	- `$T 'WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints each FACTS entry whose bold title holds them, and `$T 'section:HEADING'` every entry of a FACTS section. Run one before you investigate a behaviour of the tree, and when your brief or a note names an entry. These queries and `positions:` read titles only: before you write that the record does not hold something, also grep FACTS and POSITIONS for its words.
168	- `$T 'index:WORDS'` prints the INDEX lines that hold the words. Run it to find the notes on a topic.
169	- `$T 'ledger-find:WORDS'` prints one line for each ledger row that holds every word. Run it when you meet a defect, before you investigate it.
170	- `$T 'ledger:ROW'` prints one row whole. Run it for each row that you need from a find, your brief or a note.
171	- `$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'` prints a section of any note, or of a `.tex` chapter, and `$T 'map:FILE#HEADING'` a section of a note under `explorations/coordinator/map/`. Run one when your brief or a note names a section. `#HEADING@WORDS` prints only the table rows and list items of that section that hold every one of WORDS.
172	- `$T --check QUERY ...` prints only where each query matches and its size. Run it before a query whose size you do not know. `--part N` prints part N of a long output, and `--help` gives the rest.

196	    L="python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py"

198	To add a row:
199	
200	1. Print the row template, about 3 KB: `$T 'doc:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md#The row template'`.
201	2. Write the row as one line in a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with `?` in its number cell.
202	3. Run `$L add FILE --section TITLE`. It numbers the row and puts it in that section. If the row breaks the template, it adds nothing and prints each rule broken. `$L sections` lists the titles.

205	
206	- `$L note N TEXT` adds TEXT to the notes of row N. It refuses a note that takes the row past 1,200 characters, or its notes cell past 700 characters. `$L note N TEXT --check` writes nothing. It says whether TEXT fits, and how many characters the notes and the row have left now and would have left with TEXT. These counts include the separator that the tool adds. It exits 0 if TEXT fits, and 1 if not. Run it before a long note, or before a note on a row near its limits. If TEXT does not fit, shorten it, or cut the notes with `rewrite` (below).
207	- `$L rewrite N FILE` replaces row N with the whole line in FILE, a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with N or `?` in its number cell. Use it to correct the claim, cut the notes or change the reproducer. The tool checks the line against the template and keeps the old line in the history file.

214	- The repository is a 2018 fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository. Its trunk runs from 2007-01-04 to 2012-08-31 and ends at `a874948ac`, the team's last commit.

259	## The procedure
260	
261	1. Search the record with the queries in `records.md`. If two of the team's sources disagree, look for the construct in `revival-changes.md` before you search the record.
262	2. If the record or `revival-changes.md` settles the question, go back to building. Cite what settles it.
263	3. If you have evidence against a decision of the curator, read its POSITIONS entry and the notes that it names. If the decision used your evidence, go back to building.
264	4. Search the original tree. These help: the feature table and the phase map (`compiler.md`, "Before an edit"), the `\note{}` boxes and the map of design areas ("Weighing the sources"), and the history of a file (`records.md`, "The repository's history").

<!-- The record-landing workflow's routing writer brief: after a batch's landing, bring PLAN, PLAN-history, the review queue, INDEX and other notes in line with it in the run's worktree, as the sort assigned, with each moved line word for word; and fix them once from the checks. -->

# The routing writer of the record-landing workflow

You are a stream writer in the Fortress revival repository: a headless Opus session that takes its tasks one after another. Your standing order is the skill writer's, in your first message: its register and its writing principles hold. Its parts on skill files, on committing and on `sources.md` do not: you edit record files in the worktree, and you commit nothing. Your task names the batch, the run's folder and the worktree. The worktree is this run's own checkout, and your session runs in it: every path here is from the worktree's root.

The curator is the person in charge of the project. PLAN (`explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`) is the working plan: its phases, the curator's answers in the order the work needs them, and the parked items. `PLAN-history.md` holds, word for word, each line taken out of PLAN, under a heading for the landing that moved it. The review queue (`review-queue.md`) is the one home of each item that waits for the curator's word or review, numbered, in three parts: (b) consequential, (c) routine, (a) settled or stale. `INDEX.md` holds one line for each note. A landing is the commit that put a batch's merged work on `main`. An entry is one line of FACTS or POSITIONS under its permanent number.

## The problem

A batch has landed. PLAN still says where the work stood before it: its "Where we stand", the batch's own line in its phase, lines that the batch built or answered, and lines that no longer hold. The batch's items for the curator wait in PLAN's list for his review, or in no file. The review queue's head names the old next batch. Notes have no INDEX line. A sorter has listed what the record owes, one change per line, in `owed.md` in the run's folder. Each change has a number (C1, C2 ...), a home, a kind, a weight and its ground. Your homes are five: a PLAN line, PLAN-history, a review-queue item, an INDEX line, and a line of another note. The entries writer takes FACTS, POSITIONS, their histories and the gap ledger at the same time, in the same worktree.

## The question

For each change of `owed.md` whose writer is `routing`, what do PLAN, PLAN-history, the queue, INDEX or the note hold after it? Make the edit in the worktree, so that each file stands in line with the landing and nothing that it held is lost.

## Where the sources are

- `owed.md`, and the evidence beside it: `plan.md` (PLAN's headings with their lines, the lines that the batch added, and the other lines that name a changed entry or row), `cites.md` (the queue items and INDEX lines that name them), `rows.md`, `checks.md` (the notes without an INDEX line, and the citations of PLAN by line number) and `sources.md` (the queries of the post-batch review's routing part and of the batch record's items for the curator).
- The routing's rule: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md#After the landing'`, its step 2.
- The form of a queue item: read the queue's head and three items of one of its themes (`facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md#When each item is needed'`, and a theme's section). The form of PLAN-history's landing sections: its last one, `## Climb batch N's landing, DATE`.
- The record itself. You read it only through `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh`, `record.py` and `ledger.py`; in this session the first one runs, from the worktree: `'doc:PATH#HEADING'`, `'doc:PATH#HEADING@WORDS'` for the items of a section that hold some words, `'index:WORDS'`, `'positions:WORDS'`, `'F-87'`, `'ledger:N'`. The Edit tool needs the lines that it edits read first: open only those lines, at the line numbers that the evidence or `facts-extract.sh` gives. You write no entry: entries are written only through `record.py`, from the entries writer's file.

## How each home changes

- **A line moved.** A line that the batch built or answered, or that no longer holds, goes to `PLAN-history.md` word for word: under the landing's heading, `## Climb batch N's landing, DATE` (DATE from `git log -1 --format=%cs LANDING`), and under the heading that it stood under in PLAN. Every line that leaves PLAN or changes in it stands there word for word, since `checks.sh` compares the two files line by line.
- **A line cut to a pointer.** An open line whose whole text another home holds (a queue item, a ledger row, an entry) becomes one line in PLAN: what is asked, its default, and a pointer to that home. Its old text moves as above.
- **The batch's own line** in its phase becomes one line, with its landing commit and its post-batch review. "Where we stand" states the landing. Both keep the form that `explorations/coordinator/tools/revival-page/update.py` parses, or the workflow's last stage stops: the batch's line opens ``- **Climb batch N**, phase P's ORDINAL batch, landed YYYY-MM-DD at `COMMIT` ``, with N as the record names the batch and a second run such as `31b` on a line of its own, and the live thread says ``At the last landed gate, climb batch N's (`COMMIT` ``.
- **A queue item.** Each item for the curator that no file holds becomes one, numbered after the queue's last number, in its theme's section, in (b) if it is consequential and in (c) if it is routine, by the kind that `owed.md` gives. It says what is asked, its default as the record states it or "no default on record", the other way, its cost, its home, and its "Needed by". A "Needed by" that the batch record or the review states is taken as stated. Any other is yours, and you mark it "(set by the landing workflow)". Each section's count and the head's counts follow the items.
- **A move to (a).** An item goes to "Answered by a decision of his" only with his word on that same item, cited with its time. A default that the coordinator or a batch took is not his word. That item stays open in (b) or (c), with the default as landed, since such a decision lands and then goes to him for review (the `coordinator` skill, "The curator's role and decisions", way 2). `queue-check.py` fails a new item in that section that names such a default, or his word on another item. An item goes to "Answered by a landed fix or a closed row" only with the commit or the row that made it moot.
- **An INDEX line** for each note that `checks.md` names without one: `` - `PATH`: `` and the first sentence of the note's header comment.
- **A citation of a moved line** by its line number, in PLAN, the queue, FACTS, POSITIONS or INDEX: repoint it. `checks.md` lists them.

You invent no default and no answer of the curator. Before you call an item open, search POSITIONS and INDEX for his answer. The boot note (`BOOT.md`) and the held list (`HELD.md`) are the coordinator's: you edit neither, and you name in your report each change that they need.

## Your report

Write `routing-report.md` in the run's folder, with a header comment of one sentence: one line per change, with its number, the file and line, what you did (moved, cut to a pointer, rewritten, filed as item N, moved to (a), an INDEX line, repointed, left with its reason), and its ground. Then each "Needed by" that you set, each kind that `owed.md` marks as set by the workflow, each item that you moved to (a) with the word of his or the commit that it cites, each default that the record does not hold, and each change for the coordinator.

## The fix round

Your task says when this is your fix round. Three reports are then in the run's folder: `check.md`, the checker's, which names each failure by its change and its class (coverage, fidelity, form, routing); `cold-read.md`, which reads the entries writer's text and is not yours; and `mech-1.md`, the mechanical checks, among them `plan-moves.py` (each line out of PLAN, word for word in PLAN-history, and its `LOOK` lines, the PLAN lines that still look stale), `queue-check.py` (the numbers, the "Needed by" lines, the counts, and each item new in "Answered by a decision of his") and `check-index.sh`. Fix each failure in your five homes, as `check.md` corrects it or as the check's output shows. A doubt that no source settles keeps the file as it was, with a line in your report. Update `routing-report.md` in place. There is no second fix round.

Your final message: the files that you changed, and one line per change on what you did.

The coordinator's steps after a landing, in this order, each done whole:

1. The landing report to the curator.
   1a. The base build of the landed tree, and F-34's measure on it. The base build is a worktree at the landing commit, outside the main tree, built as "Before the launch", step 2, gives it, and then left alone. The measure runs in a scratch worktree seeded from it (`tools/seed-worktree.sh <the base build> <scratch> - <landing>`): `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/planner/codegen-measure.sh <scratch-worktree> <out-dir>` applies its patch to the worktree it is given and builds it, so it is never given the main tree or a base build (its header), about 60 s for the build and 160 s for the probe on an idle machine. Its table, its list and the comparison with F-34's last figure, declaration by declaration, are committed in one file under the batch plan's `probes/` folder, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-<N>/probes/measure-<landing>.txt`; the scratch worktree is then removed (`git -C /home/user/fortress worktree remove --force <scratch>`, since the patch leaves it edited), and F-34 takes the figure in step 3. Through climb batch 33's run 1 no stage owned the measure after a landing (`reviews/batch-33-review.md`, process finding 2); after 33b the coordinator's worker took it twelve minutes after the push, on the brief of the day (`3fbce96856`, `compile-ladder/plan-33/probes/measure-ba3c7c876d.txt`; `reviews/batch-33b-review.md`, process finding 2).
2. The routing: every open row, record default and item for the curator filed with a batch or as a parked line of `PLAN.md`. Each is checked against POSITIONS and the notes `INDEX.md` lists before it is called open, put to the curator or briefed. In the same pass the routing moves out of `PLAN.md` each item the batch built or answered, and any item it finds stale: word for word, into `PLAN-history.md`, under the landing's dated heading and the heading the item stood under. The batch's own line in its phase becomes one line, with its landing commit and its review. # The sorter of the record-landing workflow

You work in the Fortress revival repository. The curator is the person in charge of the project. The record is the project's memory under `explorations/`: `FACTS.md` and `POSITIONS.md` and their histories under `explorations/coordinator/`, the gap ledger `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`, `PLAN.md`, `PLAN-history.md`, the review queue `review-queue.md`, `INDEX.md`, and the notes. An entry is one line of FACTS or POSITIONS under its permanent number, such as F-87 or P-48. A row is one line of the gap ledger under its number.

A batch has landed: its merged work went to `main` at its landing commit. Its post-batch review is committed too. Your launch message names the batch, its base, its landing commit, the worktree and the run's folder. The worktree is this run's own checkout. Its branch takes the run's work, and the coordinator lands that branch later.

## The problem

After a landing the record owes work. The landing made some of its sentences false. The rungs wrote their entries as drafts, as the worker skill tells them: "Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work." PLAN holds lines that the batch built or answered. Items for the curator wait in PLAN, or in no file. Two writers do this work after you, and each writes only its own homes. A home is the file and the place where a change goes. In an earlier run with no sort, one tool wrote 21 findings into the text of entries, and only 8 of them belonged there. So the sort comes first, before anything is written.

## The question

What does the record owe after this landing, change by change? A change is one thing that the record owes: a sentence or a line to write, cut, move or file, or a finding that needs no change. Write each change as one line of `owed.md` in the run's folder.

## Where the sources are

First run the command that your launch message gives. It is `prepare.sh`. It makes the worktree and writes the evidence into the run's folder. Its six files: `entries.md` (each entry that the batch added or changed, its lines at the base and now, its history blocks with who wrote each, and the report sections that it cites); `rows.md` (each row that the batch opened, closed, rewrote or noted); `cites.md` (each other entry, queue item and INDEX line that names a changed entry or row); `plan.md` (PLAN's headings, the lines that the batch added, the other lines that name a changed entry or row, and the lines that look stale: a line whose own review-queue item is settled, a list of items that disagrees with the queue, a review finding that a later commit names); `checks.md` (the record's checks at the worktree's head); `sources.md` (the queries that print the review's routing part, its findings and its part for the curator, and the batch record's items for the curator and what it left for the coordinator). Read all six, and print every query of `sources.md`. The last part of `entries.md`, "The cited sections", is the entries writer's: open a section of it only where a change's ground turns on it.

You read the record only through `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh`, `record.py` and `ledger.py`, run from the worktree: `cd WORKTREE && explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'QUERY'`. The main tree, `/home/user/fortress`, can hold a later record than the worktree, so you read none of its record files. You write no entry: entries are written only through `record.py`, from the entries writer's file. Change no file but `owed.md`. Commit nothing.

## Each change

Write each change as one line, in this form:

    - C12 | home: P-N | kind: made false | weight: high | ground: <the rung's commit that closed row N; rows.md, row N> | the batch: not done | the curator's word: no, a sentence brought in line with the tree | writer: entries

- **C-number**: C1, C2 and so on. The writers, the checker and the judge name the change by it.
- **home**: one of nine. A FACTS entry (F-N); a POSITIONS entry (P-N); an entry's history only (a noted block, when the entry stays and its history lacks a fact); a gap-ledger row (row N); a PLAN line (PLAN.md:N, with its heading); a PLAN line moved to PLAN-history; a review-queue item (new, or item N); an INDEX line; a line of another note (PATH:N). Or none.
- **kind**: the pass on an entry that the batch added or changed; made false; stale; past 600 characters; built; answered; a new item for the curator; a new note.
- **weight**: high, a reader would act otherwise; low, wording or a pointer; none, no change, with the reason.
- **ground**: the file and line, the commit, or the review's section that shows the change is owed.
- **the batch**: whether a stage of the batch did it, or a part of it. `entries.md` names who wrote each history block: the gather, the merged-diff review or the commit stage.
- **the curator's word**: whether the change needs it, and why.
- **writer**: `entries` for the homes FACTS, POSITIONS, an entry's history and a row; `routing` for PLAN, PLAN-history, the queue, INDEX and other notes; `none`.

What decides a line:

- Each entry that the batch added or changed gets one change of kind "the pass", whatever else it gets. The rungs wrote it as a draft.
- Each line that `plan.md` lists as looking stale gets one change: stale, built or answered, with its ground, or weight none with the reason that it stays.
- The gate's figures in F-53 and F-240 are the commit stage's. A change keeps them, and a sentence of those entries changes only when the commit stage named it false.
- The gather closes rows. A change closes no row, and `ledger.py landing-check` must stay clean.
- A POSITIONS sentence that the tree made false changes by the fewest words, with no word of the curator: his rule of 2026-10-31. A change of what he decided, where it applies or what it requires needs his word. Name the clause and the landed fact that makes it false.
- Before you call an item for the curator open, search POSITIONS and INDEX for his answer (`positions:WORDS`, `index:WORDS`), and the ledger for a row that holds it (`ledger-find:WORDS`). An item that he answered is of kind "answered", with his word on that item's own question and its time. A default that the coordinator or a batch took is not his answer: that item stays open, of kind "a new item for the curator", with the default as landed.
- A default that the record does not hold is "no default on record". A "Needed by" that neither the batch record nor the review states is set by the workflow: mark it so, since the coordinator confirms it and the curator may change it. Mark a kind, consequential or routine, that neither of them states as "kind set by the workflow", for the same reason.
- A change of weight none stays in the file, with its reason, so that the checker can see that nothing was missed.

End `owed.md` with a section `## For the coordinator`: each change whose home is outside the record, one line each. These are the skill sentences that the batch made false (the review's part on them), the entries for the orientation update, a fault of the batch script or its manual, and any change to the boot note or the held list, which are the coordinator's.

## Your result

Your structured result: the count of changes for each home; the entries for the orientation update, the entries that the landing added or changed; and each change that needs the curator's word, with why, one line each; and a summary in a few lines.

<!-- The record-landing workflow's task for the skill writer after a landing: install the sections of the revival part that the orientation judge accepts, and bring the rest of the fortress-repo skill in line with the landing, from the landing's own list of the skill sentences that it made false; skills.sh appends the landing's data. -->

# The skill writer's task after a landing

A climb batch has landed on `main`. The record-landing workflow brought the record in line with it, landed the record's commits, and ran the orientation update. The landing made some sentences of the `fortress-repo` skill false. The data at the end of this task lists them, from the landed files, and says what the orientation update judged. Bring the skill in line with the landing.

No coordinator reads this task before you, and none rules between your steps. The data is copied from the landed files. A cold read of your commits follows, and you fix its flags in a second task.

## What to do

1. **Install the orientation's sections.** If the data says that the orientation's judge ran, read its `judgement.md`. Copy each section that it judges "install" from its `orientation.md` into `references/revival-changes.md`, word for word, in place of the section that it rewrites. A section that it holds keeps its old text. Add the lines of its `sources-mapping.md` for the installed sections to the skill's `references/sources.md`. Change nothing else in `revival-changes.md`.
2. **Bring each false sentence in line.** For each sentence that the data names, by its part and line or by its section:
   - Read the entry or the row that grounds the new truth before you touch the sentence: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'F-312'` prints one entry; `git grep -n '^| 890 ' -- explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` finds a row.
   - Find the sentence by its words. A line number in the data can be off by a few lines.
   - Change it by the fewest words that make it true, as the entry or the row states it. Check a claim about the code against the code before you write it.
   - If the data names a trap or a wall of a row that the part has no sentence for, and a worker who follows the part would fall into it, add one sentence where the part keeps its traps.
   - If a line names a term that the skill does not define, define it where the skill first uses it, in a few words, only if a worker needs it to act. If the skill does not use the term, change nothing.
   - If the sentence is already true, change nothing, and say so in your report.
3. **The changed decisions.** For each change of the curator's decisions in the data, search the skill for a sentence that rests on the old words (`git grep`). If one does, bring it in line by the fewest words. If none does, change nothing.
4. **The scope.** Edit only the `fortress-repo` skill. Change a rule's meaning only where the landing changed the tree. Add no rule that the data does not ground. A sentence of another skill that the landing made false, or that your change makes disagree, goes into your report, for the coordinator. So does a point of the data that is about how agents work rather than about the tree, such as a wait or a reading rule.

## Committing

Run `python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py` on the files you changed before each commit. Commit by named paths, as your standing brief says: one commit for `revival-changes.md` and its lines of `sources.md`, if you installed a section, and one for the other parts and their lines of `sources.md`. Open each subject with "fortress-repo:" and name the batch's landing. Do not push: the workflow pushes.

## Your report

A page worker shows each of your changes to the curator, with its reason, from your report. So give each change's reason in plain words: what the text said that was wrong, and what it now says. Name no task item, flag or ruling by its number. Then, in your standing brief's order:

- the commits, with their hashes;
- each sentence changed: its file and section, its new text, and the entry or row that grounds it;
- each section installed from the orientation, and each held one left as it was;
- each line of the data where the sentence was already true, and each that you could not place;
- each point where the record left you a choice, and each decision not taken, with its alternatives;
- each point for the coordinator: another skill's sentence, a point about how agents work, a fault of the data.

# The orientation workflow

The `fortress-repo` skill's revival part, `references/revival-changes.md`, becomes the **orientation**: the short account of how revived Fortress departs from the original and from what a model expects, which every worker reads whole (Astra's review, `explorations/reviews/revival-record-synthesis.md`). `orientation.js` writes it, in two modes:

- **consolidate**, once, and again whenever the part has drifted: an outline by the concepts workers use and a table of where each old entry goes (`outline.md`); the writer writes the whole text from them; a preservation check against the table, a cold read with only the skill's core, and the regression quiz; the writer's fix round; a second cold read and the quiz again; a judge.
- **update**, after every landing: the landing's new and changed FACTS and POSITIONS entries pass the admission test (`admission.md`: the wrong default, the correction, the mistake it prevents); the writer rewrites the sections they touch in place, within the budget of 8K to 12K characters; the same checks, fix round, reread and judge.

The writer is a headless Opus stream (`../record-clarity/writer-stream.sh`), so its fix round resumes the session that wrote the text. The regression quiz is kept in `regression/` (questions and key), and grows with each update.

## Running it

    Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/orientation/orientation.js',
               args: { mode: 'consolidate', out: '/abs/folder/', stream: 'orientation', concepts: ['/abs/concepts.md'] } })
    Workflow({ scriptPath: ..., args: { mode: 'update', out: '/abs/folder/', stream: 'orientation-bN', facts: ['F-261', 'P-153'] } })

## Installing its result

The judge writes `judgement.md` and `queue.md`. The coordinator then has the skill writer (`skill-writer.sh`) install the sections judged "install" into `references/revival-changes.md`, add `sources-mapping.md` to the skill's `references/sources.md`, and, after a consolidation, update the core's line for the part and its description together; then a cold read of the installed part, as `coordinator/references/skill-rewrite.md` says. Held sections keep the old text; their items go to `review-queue.md`.

<!-- A review of the Fortress revival's development process for dead ends in its flows of information and decisions: nine stores that fill faster than anyone empties them, each with its measured growth, its cost and a proposed fix, written for the curator on 2026-11-23. -->

# Dead ends in the flows of information and decisions, 2026-11-23

Read on `main` at `6a36bd3e6e`, at 11:3x UTC on 2026-11-23, while climb batch 35's run 1 ran. Nothing was built or run. No transcript was read: the evidence is the skills, the workflows' briefs, the record and git.

## For the curator

A dead end is a store that takes items in and has no working way to let them out.

One cause is behind most of them. Each landing runs a workflow that writes into six stores for you. Nothing but your word takes an item out. The workflow writes about 17 queue items and 11 page items a day. You answered about 3 queue items and read about 3 page items a day. The stores can only grow.

The landing's bookkeeping also costs more than the batch. Climb batch 34b's run wrote 2.0M tokens. The landing work before it wrote 4.1M.

The dead ends, in order of what they cost you:

1. **The review queue.** In 16 days, 266 items went in and about 64 went out. 185 of the 270 open items are defaults that a batch already landed. They are news, not questions.
   - Fix: a landed default is closed when it lands. You get one short report for each landing that says what changed in the language. Only a real question enters the queue, with the work that waits for it.
   - This is your "1" of today, taken one step further: the queue stops holding landed defaults at all. It needs your yes.
2. **The page of `fortress-repo` changes.** It got 172 new items in 16 days. You read 41. Most items are a sentence brought in line with the tree, not a new rule.
   - Fix: the page shows only a new rule or a changed rule. Every other change is one line with its commit. An item leaves at the next landing whether you read it or not.
   - It gives up your sight of each wording change of the worker skill. It needs your yes.
3. **The same item in up to six files.** A waiting item is copied into the batch's record, PLAN's review list, the queue's body, the queue's head, a docket and the boot note. The copies drift. On 11-17 a stale copy made the coordinator ask you a closed question (item 513).
   - Fix: one home for a question. PLAN's 37 review lists and the queue's head section go. A new sort edits the queue; it does not write a new file.
   - It needs your yes, since it changes the review list.
4. **A defect becomes a skill sentence, not a fix.** The landing workflow tells the skill writer to add a sentence for each new trap. Nothing tells a planner to fix the row. Open ledger rows went from 489 to 553 in 18 days. The worker skill grew by a quarter.
   - Fix: P-180, which you decided today, plus three mechanics: the writer adds no trap sentence; the planner gives each rung the open rows of the files that it edits; closing a row lists the skill lines to delete.
   - One point is yours: which rows P-180 binds. Options are below.
5. **Nothing teaches you what landed.** The cleanup of 11-05 wrote 117 landed decisions as "material for a page that he reads". The page was never built. You said on 11-10 that you are not learning much yet.
   - Fix: the landing report of fix 1 is that channel. It replaces the learning file.
   - It is part of fix 1.
6. **Sorts and reviews that end as a file.** The docket of 11-15 found 99 items to close and 11 contradictions. Eight days later they are still in the boot note as owed.
   - Fix: a worker that sorts a store edits the store, on a branch, as today's triage does. The coordinator lands the branch.
   - The coordinator's own change.
7. **The boot note's lists of owed work.** Some lines are 30 days old. The note is for state, and it has no step that does the work.
   - Fix: owed work goes to one housekeeping list. A housekeeping worker empties it at each landing. A line that survives two landings is done or dropped, with one line to you.
   - This is the housekeeping batch that you asked for today. The coordinator's own change.
8. **The held list.** It holds 80K characters and is read at every boot. A line leaves only at a trim.
   - Fix: each line names its exit when it is written: a decision in POSITIONS, a task for the skill writer, or an answer in chat. The line leaves when that happens.
   - It needs your yes, since it changes the held list.
9. **Stores that only cost tokens.** The skill's `sources.md` (357K) is larger than the skill. FACTS (403K) is read whole after a boot. PLAN's "Where we stand" is 15K in five bullets.
   - Fix: provenance goes in the commit message; FACTS is read by query; "Where we stand" is rewritten short at each landing.
   - The coordinator's own change.

One finding would change a decision of yours: P-180's scope (finding 4). Seven fixes change how you and the coordinator work, and wait for your yes: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, and the two rules inside 4 that touch the page. The rest are the coordinator's.

## The common cause

The record-landing workflow (`explorations/coordinator/tools/record-landing/`) runs after every landing with "no step of yours between" (`coordinator/references/batch.md`, "The landing", step 4). It is the inflow of five stores at once:

- the review queue and PLAN's review list, by its routing writer (`routing.md`, "A queue item": "Each item for the curator that no file holds becomes one");
- the `fortress-repo` skill, by its skill task and the orientation update;
- the page of `fortress-repo` changes, one item for each skill change;
- FACTS, PLAN's "Where we stand", INDEX.

Each of these stores has an exit that needs the curator: a queue item leaves "only with his word on that same item" (`routing.md`, "A move to (a)"); a page item "stays until the curator says ... that they have read it" (`skill-rewrite.md`, step 7). So the inflow is automatic and runs at the machine's speed, and the exit is manual and runs at one message a time on a phone. No rule sets a size at which the inflow stops.

The cost in tokens written, from the post-batch reviews' own spans (`explorations/reviews/batch-34b-review.md:144-146`, `batch-34-review.md:155`):

- landing work after climb batch 33: 4.80M; after 33b: 4.42M; after 34: 4.05M;
- of 34's 4.05M: the record 1.64M, the orientation update 1.40M, the skill step 0.28M, the page of `fortress-repo` changes 0.50M, the revival page 0.23M;
- climb batch 34b's whole run: 1.97M.

## The measurements

All from git, on `main`. The loop for the queue:

    f=explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md
    for h in $(git log --reverse --format=%h -- $f); do
      echo "$(git log -1 --format=%cI $h) $(git cat-file -s $h:$f) $(git show $h:$f | grep -m1 -o '\*\*Counts\*\*[^:]*')"; done

**The review queue**, open items (consequential + routine) and the file's size:

- 2026-10-20: 179 (49 + 130), 161K
- 2026-10-30: 298 (104 + 194), 438K
- 2026-11-03: 312 (107 + 205), 483K
- 2026-11-05, after the cleanup: 65 (43 + 22), 228K
- 2026-11-10: 185 (74 + 111), 428K
- 2026-11-17: 247 (92 + 155), 566K
- 2026-11-21: 270 (93 + 177), 624K

Since the cleanup the item numbers ran from 354 to 620: 266 new items in 16 days. The exits, from the counts in the headings of section (a) at `bd06be5b80` and at `8965c32e03`: "Answered by a decision of his" 63 to 109 (46, of which 35 by 11-10); "Reviewed by him as landed" 0 to 3; "Answered by a landed fix or a closed row" 43 to 58 (15). The queue's own head counts 185 of the 270 under "Climb batch N's defaults, for his review" (batches 26 to 34). The decision docket of 11-15 sorted the 200 items then open: 14 "now" (8 questions), 32 before the switch-over, 7 for speed, 141 "whenever: nothing waits on you", 6 stale.

**The page of `fortress-repo` changes**, from the saved versions in `<scratchpad>/fortress-repo-page/` (`grep -o '<section' FILE | wc -l`, less the fixed sections) and the scout's `<scratchpad>/page-archaeology/evidence.md`:

- 11-07: 12 items, 55K; 11-10: 173K; 11-16: 261K; 11-19: 135 items, 557K; 11-23: 145 items, 649K; the next item's number is 184.
- His "read" words: changes 37 and 38 on 11-08; up to 41 on 11-23.
- `git log --since=2026-11-05 --oneline -- .claude/skills/fortress-repo | wc -l`: 66 commits, 21 of them a cold read's fixes.

**The `fortress-repo` skill** without `sources.md` (`git ls-tree -r -l COMMIT -- .claude/skills/fortress-repo`): 185K on 11-05, 204K on 11-10, 230K on 11-20, 234K on 11-23. `compiler.md`: 28.5K to 47.8K. `revival-changes.md`: 19.8K to 34.1K, where the orientation workflow's README gives a budget of 8K to 12K. `sources.md`: 258K to 357K.

**The gap ledger** (`ledger.py count`; the same count over `git show COMMIT:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` by status cell):

- 11-05: 894 rows; 259 fixed; 489 open (448 `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, 12 `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, 29 `CONTESTED`).
- 11-23: 1102 rows; 397 fixed; 553 open (481, 32, 40).
- Open rows by number (`ledger.py heads`): 95 of rows 0 to 199, 94 of 200 to 399, 85 of 400 to 599, 83 of 600 to 799, 109 of 800 to 999, 87 of 1000 on. An old row is as likely to be open as a new one: age does not close rows.

**The other stores** (`git cat-file -s COMMIT:PATH` on 11-05 and on 11-23): PLAN 203K to 325K, of which "Off the path, parked" is 225K and 484 lines, with 37 lists "listed for his review"; FACTS 290K to 403K (253 to 326 entries, so 1.2K an entry against the 600-character check); the held list 57K, 129K on 11-16 before a trim, 81K now; the boot note 18K, rewritten in 1,008 commits. First dates of lines still in the boot note (`git log --reverse --format=%cs -S'WORDS' -- explorations/coordinator/BOOT.md | head -1`): the Fable judge's effort 10-20, P-75 10-23, the letter, `huge-methods.py` and the compression of three skill parts 11-10, the docket's 99 closable items 11-15.

## The findings, sorted by what each needs

### A. Would change a decision of the curator's: an ask, with options

**A1. Which rows P-180 binds (finding 4).** P-180 says that "a batch fixes the defects that make walk and the compiled path behave differently or depart from the specification". 553 rows are open, and a batch opens about 20 and closes about 14 beside its main work (208 opened and 138 fixed in 18 days). The entry does not say which of them a batch takes, so a planner cannot tell when the rule is met. The inventory (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/skill-workarounds.md`) counts 98 skill passages whose fix needs no decision, 17 of them with no row yet.

1. By the files in hand: each rung fixes the open rows that cite the files it edits and need no decision, or says in its report why one stays. The planner lists them in the rung's section. Costs each rung some of its budget; reaches every area in time; needs no extra batch.
2. By the skill: only the 98 passages of the inventory, in housekeeping batches, until the skill teaches no workaround. Then P-180 is met. Bounded and countable; leaves the 400 rows that no passage names as they are.
3. By a balance: a batch may not open more rows than it closes. The strongest reading; it can stop a batch that finds many defects, which punishes finding them.

How they weigh: 2 ends the symptom that he met and stops there; 1 changes the planning for good at a small cost per rung; 3 turns a measure into a gate. Recommendation: 2 first, as the housekeeping batch already in planning, and 1 as the standing rule after it; report 3's balance at each landing and gate nothing on it.

### B. Change how the curator and the coordinator work: for his yes to the exact words

**B1. The review queue holds landed defaults as open items (dead ends 1 and 5).**

- Enters: at each landing, the sorter and the routing writer file every fork taken at a default, every reserved point reached, every difference that the gate's comparison hid, every rewritten line of a team test (`batch.md`, "The checker count and the distance", "Reserved points and repairs"; `sort.md`: "A default that the coordinator or a batch took is not his answer: that item stays open").
- Kept: the queue's body, its head section, PLAN's review list.
- Consumed: by the curator, one per message (`SKILL.md`, way 2: "Put it to the curator later, one per message").
- Exit: his word on that item. In 16 days, 3 items left as "reviewed by him as landed".
- Cost: his attention and trust (his words of 11-02 and of today); wrong asks from stale copies (B3); about 1.6M tokens a landing for the record step; and the real questions, 8 on 11-15, are hidden among 200.
- The mismatch is in the rule, not in its execution. Way 2 treats a default as a debt that only he can clear. His own words of 06:4x on 11-17 treat it as news: "when they land, I'll review them". A review of news needs a report, not a queue.
- **Fix.** (1) In `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", way 2 becomes: a decision that can be undone lands and is closed; FACTS states it, with the words that a worker chose it; the landing report names it. (2) The landing report is one message for each landing, a list of at most about ten lines in plain words, each "what a program does differently now", most consequential first, with the FACTS number; the rest is a count. He answers a line by its number if he objects, and that objection is the only thing that opens an item. (3) The queue holds only questions: no default on record, or consequential, each with the named work that needs it. `sort.md` and `routing.md` change their "stays open" rule to "closed as landed, named in the report"; `queue-check.py` refuses a new item whose default is "as landed" unless it is consequential. (4) The 185 landed defaults now open go to the triage on `wip/queue-triage` as "closed as landed", and their accounts into one catch-up report by theme, in place of the learning file.
- Protects: his sight of the questions that the work waits on, and his learning. Costs: he no longer has a list in which each default waits for an explicit yes; a default that he would have overturned stands until he reads its line in a report. Every such default can be undone by definition, so the loss is rework, not a wrong tree.

**B2. The page of `fortress-repo` changes (dead end 2).**

- Enters: one item for each landed change of the worker skill; about 11 a day. Exit: his "read" word.
- The rule's stated purpose is in the coordinator skill: "A change that nobody reads can weaken how you and the curator work together, and nobody notices." That is true of the coordinator skill. A sentence of `compiler.md` brought in line with a closed row weakens nothing between him and the coordinator.
- **Fix.** In `skill-rewrite.md`, step 7, and `record-landing/page.md`: the page of `fortress-repo` changes holds an item only for a new rule or a change of a rule's meaning, which the writer already names as such. Every other change is one line in a list at the page's foot, with its commit's link. An item leaves at the second landing after its own, read or not; git keeps it. With finding C1 the inflow itself falls.
- Protects: his notice of a changed rule. Gives up: the page as a full, pending log of the worker skill. Saves about 0.5M tokens a landing.

**B3. One item in up to six files (dead end 3).**

- The copies: the batch's `RECORD.md`, "Items for the curator"; PLAN, "Climb batch N, listed for his review" (a paragraph each); PLAN, "Pavol's answers"; the queue's body; the queue's head, "When each item is needed" (66K); a docket; the boot note's "What waits for him", whose item 7 names about 40 items.

A dead end is a store that takes items in and has no working way to let them out.

Review written, nothing committed: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/process-review/process-dead-ends-2026-11-23.md (22K; read on `main` at `6a36bd3e6e`; no transcript read, nothing built or run).

Common cause: the record-landing workflow fills five stores at every landing, and each store's only exit is the curator's word. A landing's bookkeeping wrote 4.05M to 4.80M tokens, against 1.97M for climb batch 34b's whole run.

Dead ends, in order of cost to him, each with its fix:
1. Review queue: 266 items in and about 64 out in 16 days; 185 of the 270 open are landed defaults. Fix: close a default at its landing, name it in one landing report, and let only real questions enter the queue.
2. Page of `fortress-repo` changes: 172 new items in 16 days, 41 read. Fix: an item only for a new or changed rule, the rest one line with its commit; an item leaves at the second landing after its own.
3. One item in up to six files; the copies drift (item 513 put to him as open on 11-17). Fix: the queue is the one home; PLAN's 37 review lists and the queue's head go; a sort edits the queue.
4. A defect becomes a skill sentence, not a fix (`record-landing/skill-task.md`, step 2); open ledger rows 489 to 553, the skill 185K to 234K in 18 days. Fix: delete that rule; the planner lists the open rows of each rung's files; `ledger.py close` names the skill lines to delete; `landing-check` reports a `CONTESTED` row with no queue item.
5. Nothing teaches him what landed: the 117-item learning file never became a page. Fix: the landing report of 1.
6. Sorts and reviews end as files (the docket's 99 closable items, owed since 11-15). Fix: a worker that sorts a store edits it on a branch.
7. The boot note's owed lists, some lines 30 days old. Fix: one housekeeping list, emptied by a worker at each landing.
8. Held list, 81K at every boot. Fix: each line names its exit when written and leaves at that exit.
9. Stores that only cost tokens (`sources.md` 357K, FACTS read whole, PLAN's "Where we stand"). Fix: provenance in commit messages, FACTS by query, the section rewritten short.

Would change a decision of his: one, P-180's scope (which of the 553 open rows a batch must fix). Options: by the files a rung edits; only the inventory's 98 skill passages; or no batch opens more rows than it closes. Recommended: the 98 first as the housekeeping batch, then the files rule; report the balance and gate nothing on it.
For his yes to exact words (they change how he and the coordinator work): fixes 1 with 5, 2, 3 and 8. The coordinator's own: 4's mechanics, 6, 7, 9.
